scope: Targeted primary-source verification; not exhaustive systematic review or priority search.

core_records.title: GraphPart: homology partitioning for biological sequence analysis
core_records.supports: Homology-aware splitting, restricted single-linkage with size/class constraints, and reassignment/removal to obtain cross-fold separation.
core_records.does_not_support: Full-universe projected connected components are not the same separation target as direct pairwise separation after deleting items.

core_records.title: Constructing benchmark test sets for biological sequence analysis using independent set algorithms
core_records.supports: Explicit bridge-sequence example: single-linkage can collapse separate groups, and deleting a bridging item can permit a direct-similarity-separated split.
core_records.does_not_support: Does not establish that our Solidity lexical relation equals vulnerability-relevant dependence or that our fixed-S population ablation is unprecedented.

correction.detail: Corrects Algorithm 2 pseudocode; acknowledge if describing/implementing that algorithm.

core_records.title: How to approach machine learning-based prediction of drug/compound–target interactions
core_records.supports: Combines protein similarity, compound similarity and bioactivity edges; reports a nearly all-node giant that prevents component splits; uses community analysis and deletion to obtain smaller components.
core_records.does_not_support: Its multi-relation collapse precedent does not quantify our benchmark's coverage/representation effects. Its reported DTI predictive effects cannot be transferred to Solidity.

core_records.title: MoleculeNet: a benchmark for molecular machine learning
core_records.supports: Random, scaffold and temporal splits probe different generalization settings; 80/10/10 train/validation/test framework.
core_records.does_not_support: Scaffold identity is domain-specific, not a validated choice of Solidity clone threshold.
core_records.metadata_note: Use issue year2018; first-online date2017 does not change final9(2):513–530 citation.

core_records.title: Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure
core_records.supports: Choose blocking around intended prediction and dependence; blocking can induce extrapolation and overstate errors for an interpolation target.
core_records.does_not_support: No universally best strictness of dependence graph follows; stronger exclusion is not automatically more relevant.

core_records.title: A Comparative Study to Benchmark Cross-Project Defect Prediction Approaches
core_records.supports: Cross-project defect evaluation and reproducibility are established; benchmark replicates24 approaches across85 software products.
core_records.does_not_support: This is defect prediction, not independent evidence that project-level Solidity separation resolves clone dependence.
core_records.metadata_note: Final issue2018; Göttingen record and accepted manuscript use2017 online/acceptance date.

correction.detail: Author correction confirms statistical-analysis error changes some method rankings. Do not import original rankings; correction journal metadata is corroborated but DOI was not directly retrieved from publisher.

core_records.title: Data splitting to avoid information leakage with DataSAIL
core_records.supports: Similarity-aware splitting tied explicitly to intended deployment and OOD target; minimizes total cross-fold similarity under balancing constraints.
core_records.does_not_support: A useful similarity metric and low total leakage score do not imply our component proxy is the unique appropriate vulnerability relation.

addendum.title: Addendum: Data splitting against information leakage with DataSAIL
addendum.detail: Adds comparisons to predefined benchmark splits; maximum-similarity limits and total-similarity minimization are different objectives. No universal dominance claim.

core_records.title: Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Based on Deep Learning and Multimodal Decision Fusion
core_records.supports: Concrete smart-contract ML example explicitly reporting random70%train/30%test and averages over multiple runs.
core_records.does_not_support: The stated split alone does not prove contamination or quantify inflation; do not accuse this study of either without auditing its files.

core_records.title: A Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Method Based on Heterogeneous Contract Semantic Graphs and Pre-Training Techniques
core_records.supports: Concrete smart-contract ML example reports random70/20/10 split after comment removal, short-file filtering and duplicate-contract removal.
core_records.does_not_support: Random splitting after some deduplication is not proof of remaining leakage; it illustrates why deduplication scope and grouping must be specified.
